assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining GLP-1 as an incretin and turning it into therapies that transformed diabetes and obesity treatment is a clear, original, high-impact discovery-to-medicine arc with large lasting clinical and physiological consequences.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of the proglucagon-derived peptide), Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 form and its synthesis) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology and receptor agonist concept) form a plausible trio; Knudsen's industrial drug-development role and other early contributors (for example Habener) are not fully reflected in the supplied credit, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in large randomized trials and mass clinical use; recognition is timely and arguably urgent.
uncertainties: Allocation among academic discoverers versus drug developers is unresolved and the list omits some early contributors.
I am relying on my own knowledge of the history and have not independently verified priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells that durably eradicate refractory B-cell malignancies represent a new therapeutic modality with strong originality and demonstrated clinical effect.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with costimulatory domains), Sadelain (CAR design with CD28 costimulation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified lymphocyte trials) are a reasonable trio; the original chimeric receptor concept by others (for example Eshhar) is not among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long-term remissions are established; limitations in solid tumors and toxicity do not undermine the core discovery. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric-receptor concept is not in the supplied names.
Durability of cures and long-term safety are still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established the proof of principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, converting CML from a fatal to a chronic disease; the concept and its clarity are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound program), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof in CML) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a natural trio; the chemistry contribution within Novartis and the earlier Rowley/Witte discoveries complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of outcome data and many successor kinase inhibitors; recognition is somewhat overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Upstream Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discoveries are partly credited elsewhere.
Whether the prize would be seen as primarily a drug development rather than discovery award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a fundamentally new intracellular signaling pathway from ER to nucleus, with wide relevance to physiology, secretory cell function, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori jointly delineated the Ire1/Hac1 (HAC1 splicing and transcriptional program) pathway through complementary work, supporting a clean two-person configuration; other contributors (for example Ron on the PERK arm) are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed across species and has matured over three decades; clinical translation is still developing, but fundamental impact is solid.
uncertainties: Contributions of the PERK/ATF6 branches are outside the credited names.
Clinical consequences are less direct than for therapeutic candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines prevent infection and cervical and other cancers; the combination of a clever structural insight and enormous public-health consequence is compelling.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (early VLP/L1-L2 work with Zhou) are credible; others (for example Kirnbauer, Zhou) are partly excluded, and prior recognition of HPV-cancer linkage (zur Hausen) is a separate matter.
assessment.maturity: Population-level reductions in HPV infection and cervical precancer are well documented, with emerging cancer-incidence data; timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Priority disputes between groups are difficult to resolve from the supplied names.
Contested patent history may affect perception of attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general method for causal control of defined cell populations, reshaping neuroscience experimentation; it is original and broadly enabling, though its impact is principally as a tool.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin identification and characterization), Deisseroth (neuronal implementation and in vivo use), with Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck as other strong contributors; a three-person limit makes the allocation difficult and contentious.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for more than a decade; clinical translation (vision restoration) is emerging, so recognition is mature in basic research.
uncertainties: More than three plausible laureates; any trio leaves out major contributors.
Methodological versus physiological discovery framing may count against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PCSK9 links human genetics to a validated lipid-lowering target and a new drug class, a particularly clear example of human-genetics-to-therapy translation.
assessment.attribution: Seidah (discovery and biochemistry of PCSK9), Hobbs and Cohen (loss-of-function variants and lipid lowering in humans) form a coherent trio; Abifadel/Boileau (first gain-of-function mutations in hypercholesterolemia) have a strong competing claim.
assessment.maturity: Approved PCSK9 inhibitors with outcome-trial data; the core mechanism is confirmed. Prize-worthiness is strong but narrower than other candidates.
uncertainties: Competition between gain-of-function discovery and loss-of-function validation.
Overall field impact smaller than broad physiological discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR defined a central regulator of cell growth and metabolism that links nutrient signals to growth control, with importance across cancer, aging, immunology and metabolism.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and established its function; Schreiber's work on rapamycin-FKBP12 and the identification of mTOR as its target is also essential; the work of Sabatini and others on mTORC1 is partly left out here.
assessment.maturity: Pathway is extensively confirmed, with clinical use of rapalogs; interpretation is stable though mTOR network understanding keeps evolving.
uncertainties: Division of credit among yeast genetics, drug-target identification and mammalian pathway work is unclear.
Allegations or controversy concerning a credited individual's conduct, if relevant, were not evaluated.
